questions.question_text:
Consider a computer with a 4 MHz processor. Its DMA controller can transfer
8 bytes in 1 cycle from a device to main memory through cycle stealing at regular
intervals. Which one of the following is the data transfer rate (in bits per second) of
the DMA controller if 1% of the processor cycles are used for DMA?
questions.subtopic: I/O interface: interrupt and DMA mode
questions.explaination: Processor clock frequency is $4\text{ MHz} = 4 \times 10^6$ cycles/s. DMA steals 1\% of cycles $= 0.01 \times 4 \times 10^6 = 40,000$ cycles/s. In each stolen cycle, 8 bytes ($8 \times 8 = 64$ bits) are transferred. Transfer rate $= 40,000 \times 64 = 2,560,000$ bps $= 25,60,000$ bps.

Which one of the following is the data transfer rate (in bits per second) of the DMA controller if 1\% of the processor cycles are used for DMA?

IEEE 754 standard is:
Sign
(1bit)

Organizing Institute: IISc, Bengaluru

questions.subtopic: Number representations and computer arithmetic (fixed and floating point)
questions.explaination: In IEEE 754 single precision: sign bit 0 means positive. The exponent field 11111111 is reserved for $\pm\infty$ and NaN. The largest finite representable number has the maximum non-reserved biased exponent, which is $254 = 11111110_2$, with all mantissa bits set to 1 ($111\dots1$), corresponding to option B.

Let 𝑇(𝑛) be the recurrence relation defined as follows:
𝑇(0) = 1,
𝑇(1) = 2, and
𝑇(𝑛) = 5𝑇(𝑛−1) −6𝑇(𝑛−2) for 𝑛≥2

Which one of the following statements is TRUE?

options.D: 𝑇(𝑛) = ⁡Θ(𝑛3𝑛)

questions.subtopic: Combinatorics: counting, recurrence relations, generating functions
questions.explaination: The characteristic equation is $r^2 - 5r + 6 = 0 \implies (r - 2)(r - 3) = 0$, with roots $r = 2, 3$. The general solution is $T(n) = c_1 2^n + c_2 3^n$. Using initial conditions $T(0) = 1, T(1) = 2$: $c_1 + c_2 = 1$ and $2c_1 + 3c_2 = 2 \implies c_1 = 1, c_2 = 0$. Thus, $T(n) = 2^n = \Theta(2^n)$.

Let 𝑓(𝑥) be a continuous function from ℝ to ℝ such that
𝑓(𝑥) = 1 −𝑓(2 −𝑥)
Which one of the following options is the CORRECT value of ∫𝑓(𝑥)𝑑𝑥
2
0
?

options.D:
−1

Organizing Institute: IISc, Bengaluru

questions.explaination: Let $I = \int_0^2 f(x) \, dx$. Using the property $\int_0^a f(x) \, dx = \int_0^a f(a - x) \, dx$, $I = \int_0^2 f(2 - x) \, dx$. Adding both gives $2I = \int_0^2 [f(x) + f(2 - x)] \, dx$. Since $f(x) + f(2 - x) = 1$, we have $2I = \int_0^2 1 \, dx = 2 \implies I = 1$.

questions.question_text:
Let 𝐴 be the adjacency matrix of a simple undirected graph 𝐺. Suppose 𝐴 is its own
inverse. Which one of the following statements is always TRUE?

options.D: There is no such graph 𝐺

questions.explaination: If $A = A^{-1}$, then $A^2 = I$. The $(i, j)$-th entry of $A^2$ is the number of walks of length 2 between vertex $i$ and vertex $j$. Thus $(A^2)_{ii} = \text{deg}(i) = 1$ for every vertex $i$, and $(A^2)_{ij} = 0$ for $i \neq j$. Every vertex has degree exactly 1, which defines a 1-regular graph, i.e., a perfect matching.

questions.question_text:
When six unbiased dice are rolled simultaneously, the probability of getting all
distinct numbers (i.e., 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6) is

options.D:
11
324

Organizing Institute: IISc, Bengaluru

questions.explaination: When six unbiased 6-faced dice are rolled, total outcomes are $6^6$. The number of outcomes where all 6 faces are distinct is $6! = 720$. The probability is $\frac{6!}{6^6} = \frac{720}{46656} = \frac{5}{324}$.

model, which one of the following statements is TRUE?

options.A: The weak entity set MUST have total participation in the identifying relationship
options.B: The owner entity set MUST have total participation in the identifying relationship

questions.question_text:
Node X has a TCP connection open to node Y. The packets from X to Y go through
an intermediate IP router R. Ethernet switch S is the first switch on the network path
between X and R. Consider a packet sent from X to Y over this connection.
Which of the following statements is/are TRUE about the destination IP and MAC
addresses on this packet at the time it leaves X?

options.A: The destination IP address is the IP address of R
options.B: The destination IP address is the IP address of Y
options.C: The destination MAC address is the MAC address of S
options.D: The destination MAC address is the MAC address of Y

questions.subtopic: Concept of layering: OSI and TCP/IP Protocol Stacks
questions.explaination: In an end-to-end IP network, the destination IP address remains invariant throughout transit and is always the IP address of final host Y. The destination MAC address changes hop-by-hop and is set to the MAC address of the next-hop router R (not switch S, which operates transparently at Layer 2).

Which of the following tasks is/are the responsibility/responsibilities of the memory
management unit (MMU) in a system with paging-based memory management?

options.A: Allocate a new page table for a newly created process
options.B: Translate a virtual address to a physical address using the page table

options.D:
Raise a trap when a process tries to write to a page marked with read-only

Organizing Institute: IISc, Bengaluru

Page table allocation (A) is an OS kernel duty.

questions.question_text:
Consider a process P running on a CPU. Which one or more of the following events
will always trigger a context switch by the OS that results in process P moving to a
non-running state (e.g., ready, blocked)?

options.A: P makes a blocking system call to read a block of data from the disk
options.B: P tries to access a page that is in the swap space, triggering a page fault
options.C: An interrupt is raised by the disk to deliver data requested by some other process
options.D: A timer interrupt is raised by the hardware

questions.subtopic: System calls, processes, threads, inter-process communication
questions.explaination: When process P executes a blocking I/O system call, it must wait for disk transfer and is moved to the blocked state (A). When P experiences a page fault on a swapped page, it is put into the blocked state until disk I/O completes (B). Interrupts from other devices (C) or timer ticks (D) in preemptive systems might return directly to P after ISR handling if P has highest priority.

Which of the following statements about the Two Phase Locking (2PL) protocol
is/are TRUE?

options.B:
With 2PL, a transaction always locks the data item being read or written just
before every operation and always releases the lock just after the operation
options.C:
With 2PL, once a lock is released on any data item inside a transaction, no more
locks on any data item can be obtained inside that transaction
options.D: A deadlock is possible with 2PL

questions.explaination: Two-Phase Locking (2PL) guarantees conflict serializability (A). In 2PL, once a lock is released (shrinking phase), no new locks can be acquired (C). Basic 2PL is susceptible to deadlocks due to circular wait conditions (D). Statement B describes conservative/static locking, not general 2PL.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about IPv4 fragmentation is/are TRUE?

options.A:
The fragmentation of an IP datagram is performed only at the source of the
datagram
options.B:
The fragmentation of an IP datagram is performed at any IP router which finds
that the size of the datagram to be transmitted exceeds the MTU
options.C: The reassembly of fragments is performed only at the destination of the datagram
options.D:
The reassembly of fragments is performed at all intermediate routers along the
path from the source to the destination

Organizing Institute: IISc, Bengaluru

questions.explaination: In IPv4, any intermediate router encountering a packet larger than the outgoing link MTU performs fragmentation (B). In contrast, fragment reassembly is performed strictly at the final destination host (C) to prevent re-fragmentation overhead and handle out-of-order routing.

questions.question_text:
An instruction format has the following structure:
Instruction Number: Opcode destination reg, source reg-1, source reg-2
Consider the following sequence of instructions to be executed in a pipelined
processor:
I1: DIV R3, R1, R2
I2: SUB R5, R3, R4
I3: ADD R3, R5, R6
I4: MUL R7, R3, R8
Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?

options.A: There is a RAW dependency on R3 between I1 and I2
options.B: There is a WAR dependency on R3 between I1 and I3
options.C: There is a RAW dependency on R3 between I2 and I3
options.D:
There is a WAW dependency on R3 between I3 and I4

Organizing Institute: IISc, Bengaluru

questions.explaination: In I1: `DIV R3, R1, R2` (writes R3); I2: `SUB R5, R3, R4` (reads R3). Since I2 reads R3 after I1 writes R3, this is a Read-After-Write (RAW) data dependency on R3 between I1 and I2 (A is true). I3 writes R3, so between I1 (write) and I3 (write) is WAW, and between I2 (read) and I3 (write) is WAR.

Which of the following fields of an IP header is/are always modified by any router
before it forwards the IP packet?

options.D: Header Checksum

questions.subtopic: Fragmentation and IP addressing, IPv4, CIDR notation
questions.explaination: Whenever an IP packet is processed by an intermediate router, its Time to Live (TTL) field is decremented by at least 1. Because the header content changes, the router must recompute and update the Header Checksum field. Source and Protocol remain unchanged.

Elements 1 and 3 must precede 2, while 3 must precede 4. Counting topological orderings of $\{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ satisfying these constraints yields exactly 5 total orders: (1,3,2,4), (1,3,4,2), (3,1,2,4), (3,1,4,2), (3,4,1,2).

questions.question_text:
Let 𝐴⁡be an array containing integer values. The distance of 𝐴 is defined as the
minimum number of elements in 𝐴 that must be replaced with another integer so
that the resulting array is sorted in non-decreasing order. The distance of the array
[2, 5, 3, 1, 4, 2, 6] is ___________

Organizing Institute: IISc, Bengaluru
questions.explaination: To minimize replacements to make array $A$ sorted in non-decreasing order, keep the longest non-decreasing subsequence (LNDS). For $A = [2, 5, 3, 1, 4, 2, 6]$, a longest non-decreasing subsequence is $[2, 3, 4, 6]$ of length 4. The minimum elements to replace is $n - \text{length(LNDS)} = 7 - 4 = 3$.
